pages.heading: Top 10 sport moments of 2026
pages.body: Chosen by UBP from published coverage. Good news only. Not an official ranking.

items.title: Katie Taylor says goodbye at Croke Park
items.blurb: Katie Taylor wins her last fight at Croke Park before more than 80,000 fans.

items.title: Mayo win the All-Ireland
items.blurb: Mayo beat Kerry to win a fourth All-Ireland title, 75 years after their third.

items.title: Rory McIlroy retains the Masters
items.blurb: Rory McIlroy retains the Masters, finishing one shot clear of Scottie Scheffler.

items.title: Galway win the ladies football final
items.blurb: Galway win the All-Ireland ladies football title for the first time since 2004.

items.title: Cork win the camogie final
items.blurb: Cork edge Galway by a point before a record 33,419 camogie crowd.

items.title: Mark English and Rhasidat Adeleke in Birmingham
items.blurb: Mark English wins European 800m gold and Rhasidat Adeleke 200m silver on one night.

items.title: Kate O'Connor is European heptathlon champion
items.blurb: Kate O'Connor wins European heptathlon gold in Birmingham with 6,751 points.

items.title: Limerick win the All-Ireland hurling final
items.blurb: Limerick beat Galway to win the All-Ireland hurling final on 19 July.

items.title: Troy Parrott and the night in Prague
items.blurb: We did not get there, but that flicker of hope brought the nation together.

items.title: Ben Lynch reaches an Olympic final
items.blurb: Ben Lynch becomes the first Irish skier in an Olympic final and finishes eighth.

pages.heading: Top 10 big moments for the country
pages.body: Chosen by UBP from published coverage. Good news only. Not an official ranking.

items.title: Jessie Buckley wins an Oscar
items.blurb: Jessie Buckley becomes the first Irish winner of the Best Actress Oscar for Hamnet.

items.title: Katie Taylor's farewell
items.blurb: Katie Taylor retires as a three time undisputed world champion at Croke Park.

items.title: Mayo end the wait
items.blurb: Mayo win their fourth All-Ireland football title, the first since 1951.

items.title: Solar power surges
items.blurb: Grid solar tops 1 gigawatt in April. Installed solar passes 3 gigawatts by August.

items.title: A record crowd for camogie
items.blurb: A record 33,419 fans watch the camogie final at Croke Park.

items.title: A record Leaving Cert year
items.blurb: Leaving Cert participation hits a record 70,411, the highest in the exam's 100 year history.

items.title: U2 are back at number one
items.blurb: U2 score their eleventh Irish number one album with Carnaval De Luz.

items.title: First graduates of an inclusive programme
items.blurb: Twelve students become the first graduates of TU Dublin's Independent Living Skills programme.

items.title: Student fee cut
items.blurb: Budget 2027 cuts the student contribution by 150 euro, to 2,350 euro.

items.title: Apprenticeships keep growing
items.blurb: Ireland now has 30,536 apprentices working with 10,191 companies.

pages.heading: Top 10 Irish songs and albums of 2026
pages.body: Built from the weekly IRMA charts up to 20 November 2026. The year end charts are not out yet.

items.title: Amble: The Swell
items.blurb: First Irish number one single, ending an eleven week run by Rein Me In.

items.title: Kingfishr: The Sun Will Never Settle
items.blurb: Their second Irish number one single, after Killeagh's 17 weeks on top.

items.title: Fontaines D.C.: Dopamine Chamber
items.blurb: Goes to number one on the Irish albums chart, their second chart topper.

items.title: U2: Carnaval De Luz
items.blurb: Their eleventh Irish number one album, and first new album in nine years.

items.title: Dermot Kennedy: The Weight of the Woods
items.blurb: Debuts at number one, his third Irish chart topper in a row.

items.title: Niall Horan: Dinner Party
items.blurb: Debuts at number one, his fourth Irish number one album in a row.

items.title: CMAT: Euro-Country
items.blurb: Wins the Ivor Novello for Best Album, her first Ivor win.

items.title: Keywest: One More For The Road
items.blurb: Number one on the Irish albums chart as a CD only release.

items.title: BASHT.: Poor Advice
items.blurb: Debut album tops the Independent chart and enters the main chart at number seven.

items.title: The Mary Wallopers: Paddywhackery
items.blurb: Trad folk album enters the Irish chart at number four.

pages.heading: Top 10 Irish films and TV of 2026
pages.body: Based on the 2026 IFTAs, the Oscars and the Irish Examiner mid year lists. Not an official ranking.

items.title: Hamnet
items.blurb: Jessie Buckley wins the Oscar for Hamnet, which also took four IFTAs.

items.title: Christy
items.blurb: Christy wins Best Film at the IFTAs, plus Director, Casting and Editing.

items.title: Blue Lights
items.blurb: Blue Lights, in its third series, wins Best Drama at the IFTAs.

items.title: Saipan
items.blurb: Éanna Hardwicke wins the IFTA for Lead Actor as Roy Keane in Saipan.

items.title: House of Guinness
items.blurb: Anthony Boyle wins Lead Actor in a Drama at the IFTAs for House of Guinness.

items.title: Trespasses
items.blurb: Trespasses wins IFTAs for script, lead performance in a drama, and makeup and hair.

items.title: Avatar: Fire and Ash
items.blurb: Tallaght's Richard Baneham wins his third Oscar, for the effects in Avatar: Fire and Ash.

items.title: Hokum
items.blurb: Damian McCarthy's horror Hokum, shot in West Cork, stars Adam Scott.

items.title: Power Ballad
items.blurb: John Carney's comedy Power Ballad stars Paul Rudd as a wedding singer.

items.title: A Quiet Love
items.blurb: A Quiet Love, told entirely in Irish Sign Language, is on RTÉ Player.

pages.heading: Top 10 Irish creators (female)
pages.body: Chosen by UBP from published rankings and coverage. In no particular order, so not a ranking. These ten are also the nominees for the UBP Awards creator category. Follower counts are from official profiles on 23 November 2026 unless dated otherwise.

items.title: Alice Kelly
items.blurb: Kildare baker with over 2 million followers. Her debut cookbook came out July 2026.

items.title: Fiona Bergin
items.blurb: Kilkenny farming creator with about 458,000 followers. Face of Agri Aware's 2025 farm safety campaign.

items.title: Jane Ní Luasa (Gaeilge le Jane)
items.blurb: Raised in the Cork Gaeltacht, she teaches Irish online. 71,900 followers.

items.title: Justine Stafford
items.blurb: Meath comedian, writer and presenter known for character sketches. 332,200 followers.

items.title: Kayleigh Trappe
items.blurb: Monaghan comedian whose lip syncs and skits make Ireland laugh. 217,400 followers.

items.title: Lauren Whelan
items.blurb: Carlow creator of makeup, hair and style videos. 1.7 million followers.

items.title: Mary-Claire Fitzpatrick
items.blurb: Laois comedian and presenter with a new 2026 podcast, Herself and Herself. 199,600 followers.

items.title: Maura Higgins
items.blurb: Longford creator and presenter named to TIME100 Creators 2026. 1.6 million TikTok followers.

items.title: Miriam Mullins
items.blurb: Cork comedy skits, lip syncs and lifestyle videos. 2.2 million TikTok followers.

items.title: Roz Purcell
items.blurb: Tipperary broadcaster and Hike Life author who spotlighted her home county for Fáilte Ireland.

pages.heading: Top 10 Irish creators (male)
pages.body: Chosen by UBP from published rankings and coverage. In no particular order, so not a ranking. These ten are also the nominees for the UBP Awards creator category. Cairde and the Gardiner Brothers are groups of lads, so they sit here. Follower counts are from official profiles on 23 November 2026 unless dated otherwise.

items.title: Cairde
items.blurb: Seven Irish dancers from Clare, Cork and Galway. 3.2 million TikTok followers.

items.title: Cian Twomey
items.blurb: Cork sketch comedian famous for his Emily character videos. About 6 million Facebook followers.

items.title: Ciaran McDonnell
items.blurb: Comedy skits and accent videos. About 967,000 TikTok followers.

items.title: Eric Roberts
items.blurb: Donegal comedy and lifestyle creator and children's author. 796,000 TikTok followers.

items.title: Gardiner Brothers
items.blurb: Irish dancing brothers raised in Galway. 4.1 million TikTok followers.

items.title: James Doyle (Protein Bor Papi)
items.blurb: Mullingar fitness creator behind the Protein Bor catchphrase. More than 1.7 million TikTok followers.

items.title: John Nellis
items.blurb: Football creator from Newcastle, County Down, and 2026 Strictly contestant. 2.6 million TikTok followers.

items.title: Matthew Weldon
items.blurb: Dublin antique jeweller sharing tips and facts. 216,300 TikTok followers.

items.title: Séaghan Ó Súilleabháin (The Kerry Cowboy)
items.blurb: Kerry farmer sharing farm life and Irish language and culture. 213,700 TikTok followers.

items.title: Tadhg Fleming
items.blurb: Kerry comedy creator known for skits with his dad. 3.1 million TikTok followers.

pages.heading: Top 10 positive moments of 2026
pages.body: Ten good news moments confirmed in published coverage. Chosen by UBP, not a public ranking.

items.title: Rock Choir sings Dreams at the Giant's Causeway
items.blurb: More than 500 singers, over 10 million views, and praise from The Cranberries.

items.title: Youth Night lights up the country
items.blurb: Youth clubs across Ireland open their doors for Oíche na hÓige on 13 November.

items.title: Gardiner Brothers keep dancing
items.blurb: Galway dancers who went viral worldwide now have about 4.1M TikTok followers.

items.title: Pint of Plane
items.blurb: A Cork woodworker restoring old tools has about 3.5M TikTok followers.

items.title: Jazzy and Calvin Harris
items.blurb: Satisfy reached number nine on the UK Official Trending Chart.

items.title: Kettama at Coachella
items.blurb: Irish DJ Kettama played Coachella in 2026 and charted in the UK.

items.title: Children of Prague
items.blurb: RTÉ said the fans' singing in Prague became a tourist attraction.

items.title: Irish students win on the world stage
items.blurb: TU Dublin's SolHex win a world business plan competition in May.

items.title: LauraLynn 24 Hour Challenge
items.blurb: Over 700 people raised 205,995 euro in 24 hours for children's palliative care.

items.title: Athletics Ireland hits a record
items.blurb: Athletics Ireland reaches an all time high of 76,507 registered members.
